answer: A marketplace can resist sybils by making every identity post a refundable bond that sits in escrow like water held behind a canyon dam: the bond is only released after a long season of honest trades, and a random audit samples a fraction of all deals. A fake identity that cheats once loses its whole bond, so an attacker running a garden of sock puppets must fund each one in full and still faces the audit lottery on every trade. The inlet for new agents stays open — anyone can join — but the price of admission is real capital at risk, not a free username.
